claims.text: Mechanical-property differences between equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi and its ternary or quaternary subsets are governed by SFE-dependent changes in the balance between dislocation slip and deformation twinning.
Equiatomic CrCoNi has a lower effective SFE than equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi.
Low SFE in CrCoNi gives it a high propensity for deformation twinning.
CrCoNi develops a more extensive, stable, three-dimensional twin network than the quinary baseline.
Deformation twins impede dislocation motion and thereby increase strength and strain hardening.
The twin network provides multiple pathways for plastic flow and thereby maintains ductility.
Twinning-controlled deformation in CrCoNi is associated with a favorable combination of strength, ductility, and fracture toughness.
Equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi and equiatomic CrCoNi can both form single-phase FCC microstructures.
Identical arc-melting, annealing, and controlled cooling will ensure homogeneous and directly comparable microstructures across the candidate alloys.
Removing Mn and Fe from equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi to produce equiatomic CrCoNi can alter SFE without introducing a secondary phase.
CrCoNi will exhibit a higher deformation-twin density than CrMnFeCoNi under identical loading conditions.
CrCoNi will exhibit a higher strain-hardening rate than CrMnFeCoNi under identical loading conditions.
CrCoNi has a better strength-ductility combination than the equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi baseline, particularly at cryogenic temperature.
Selected quaternary subsets will generally show higher twin density, strain hardening, and strength-ductility balance than CrMnFeCoNi.
Deformation nanotwinning becomes more prominent at cryogenic temperatures, where strength, ductility, and toughness can be maintained or enhanced.
The equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi baseline has a lower twin density and slightly lower strain hardening than the reduced-component alloys.
The hypothesis is limited to processing and testing regimes in which the compared alloys remain single-phase FCC.
The quantitative contribution of deformation twinning to strengthening and plasticity in CrCoNi remains uncertain.
Solid-solution strengthening and other microstructural mechanisms may also contribute to the observed property differences.
